CODED and NDFI, Tmask, SOM clustering and the agreement of change maps (phase 18)
Five more Zeit tools, all through Zeit 0.52.1's public API and with no new dependency in the runtime:

ul: CODED (zeit.coded): forest degradation and deforestation from the NDFI of every observation; strata (forest, non-forest, degradation, deforestation, disturbance, in a colormap of their own), first and last change dates, NDFI change, mean NDFI of the training period. Without training points, forest is told by the NDFI (0.5), so scikit-learn is not needed. On the chart: the changes, and the NDFI with the training mean when the layer shows a normalized difference.
NDFI (zeit.unmix): the NDFI of every date (and, if asked, the GV, NPV, soil and shade fractions) as a series that opens as a new layer.
Tmask (zeit.tmask): clouds and shadows the quality band missed, marked on the chart; the series shown without them as a new layer.
SOM clustering (zeit.som): trained on a sample of the area, every pixel goes to the nearest neuron; the chart draws the typical series of the cluster under the cursor, in its colour.

Agreement of change maps (zeit.agreement): on two or more maps of dates Janus already shows (LandTrendr, CCDC, BFAST, CODED...), from any layer, put on the grid of the first: consensus year, how many maps agree.

blocks.p: The bridge gained what they need, and the C++ stays generic: series outputs (one band per date, Janus's date labels in the band descriptions, Int16 with a scale when it fits), opened as layers without taking the active one; a fit step on rows spread over the window before the chunks, whose model reaches every chunk and may add classes and their typical series to the result (its time is part of the estimate); tools on result maps (a "layers" parameter, filtered by unit); outputs written only when a parameter is on.

Fix: CCDC's automatic reflectance units were decided again in every chunk (each window gets a copy of ctx), not once per run; a cache shared by the copies keeps the decision. The units moved to zeit_common for CCDC, NDFI, CODED and Tmask.

Self-tests: make_selftest_data.py makes a monthly Landsat-style series with a degradation, a clearing and haze Fmask misses, run in CI with --selftest-zeit, which now checks that series outputs open with the same dates and runs the agreement on the maps of dates the other tools made. --selftest-ui loads a finished run: the series becomes a layer and the active one stays, the class map comes with its typical series.
export fixed and with shortcuts, embeddings and a run's outputs as GeoTIFF, layout reset

The export options popup (File > Export map as PNG, values, rendered view) was never drawn: uiExport() was defined in 0.19.0 but not called, so the menu items opened nothing. The self-tests called exportPng and the others directly; --selftest-ui now types the shortcuts (ImGui key events) and checks that each popup opens, which fails without the fix.

File > Export embeddings as GeoTIFF (Ctrl+Shift+M) writes the view shown, over the visible area or the whole layer, as Float32 on the layer's own grid and CRS, computed again at full resolution from the files rather than the Int8 store: the six principal component scores (not stretched, named with their share of the variance), the cosine similarity to the reference, or the cosine distance between the years; model, year, licence and attribution go in the metadata. --selftest-embeddings-ui checks each file against the image shown (within the store's Int8 steps).

The store's Int8 range of each dimension came from blocks of the middle year only: 60% of AlphaEarth's 2024 vectors had a dimension clipped. It now comes from a sample of every year (each at other places of the image, 65 536 vectors in all); the self-test fails if more than 10% of the sampled vectors reach the range's ends.

Zeit results: Save all outputs of this run (right click a result, File > Export Zeit result, Ctrl+Shift+S) copies every output of the run, e.g. the seven of LandTrendr, into a folder at once, warning before replacing a file; files are named <layer>_<tool>_<output>.tif. Ctrl+S saves the result drawn on top.

Shortcuts: Ctrl+E map as PNG, Ctrl+Shift+E values, Ctrl+Shift+V rendered view, Ctrl+J the Exports window (Command on a Mac); none with Ctrl+Alt, which is AltGr on many keyboards. They do nothing while an options popup is open.

View > Reset layout (Ctrl+Shift+R) docks every panel as at the first start, puts the floating windows (Exports, Tasks, Log, Settings) back at their first size and place, also from another monitor, and the map panels to the right of the main map; open panels stay open. Checked in --selftest-ui. --selftest-embeddings-ui no longer saves the user's layout.
embeddings (AlphaEarth, TESSERA), phase 17

Layers of foundation-model embeddings (one vector per 10 m pixel and year) are drawn through their principal components as RGB (one PCA for every year, so colours mean the same in each; or local to the ROI, fitted again as it moves), the cosine similarity to the cursor, a pin or the ROI mean, and the change between years. They open from a folder of yearly GeoTIFFs, a single GeoTIFF of one year, or zeit.save_raster's file of every year (Layer::bandBase: a date's bands may be a block of a file); Zeit's temporal tools are disabled on them.

Everything is computed in C++: every year kept as Int8 with a scale per dimension, read block by block at full resolution in the file's type (GDAL reads pixel-interleaved files band by band otherwise: 8 years of TESSERA took 31 s, now 4 s); the covariance of up to 65 536 vectors with SIMD kernels chosen at run time (AVX2 + FMA, SSE2, NEON), the leading eigenvectors by subspace iteration, images by Int8 dot products with the scale, mean and stretch folded into the weights. A PCA of 128 dimensions takes about 10 ms and an image of 1 Mpx about 4 ms; it matches a plain double-precision PCA of the same sample.

The Embeddings panel holds the views, the components and stretch, the reference, the similarity of the cursor and pins over the years and their latent profiles. The Layers panel adds the embeddings of the visible area or the ROI over any series, as the basemap: a Zeit job (task_embeddings.py) writes Int16 GeoTIFFs, a bar on the map shows its progress and the layer comes on top, reprojected if needed, while the series stays active.

The runtime gains zarr, obstore, numcodecs, pyarrow, requests and shapely, with geotessera and geopandas installed without their dependencies. drawImage can sample nearest (embedding pixels), also on Metal. --selftest-embeddings checks the kernels and the PCA with timings (also in CI); --selftest-embeddings-ui checks every view, or downloads the embeddings of a series' visible area and checks them over it.

blocks.p: faster Zeit raster jobs

ul: The bridge reads the next row band in a thread while the tool computes the current one (GDAL reads without the GIL), and the outputs are compressed on the job's threads (GTiff NUM_THREADS); reads go straight to float64 (no float32 copy on the way).
Measured side by side (3000x3000 x 41 dates, Float32 LZW): Mann-Kendall 1.75-1.95x faster, LandTrendr 1.2-1.25x; outputs identical bit for bit (CCDC in 12 bands with band roles and Fmask too).
Inputs.read returns each band's own ctx (bands, Fmask), so a band read ahead never overwrites the one being computed.

Cursor, pins, other layers' series, ROI, tile requests and the view use the exact PROJ transformation.
The ROI applies to every visible layer, with its mean and p10-p90 on the chart and a column per layer in the Statistics panel.
Self-test and CI: F, a series in another CRS reprojected over B.

blocks.p: tsv is now Janus; command line: jn

ul: The program is Janus: window, app (Janus.app, io.github.sacridini.janus), installer, Start menu, "Open in Janus", Linux .desktop, release files (janus-<version>-*), executable janus. The command line is jn: jn.com on Windows (it starts janus.exe next to it), a link to the program elsewhere (in the Linux package; README for macOS).
Data folders move to Janus's the first time it starts (Application Support/Janus, Caches/Janus, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Janus, ~/.local/share/janus), cached overviews included (.tsvcube -> .januscube).
The Windows installer has a new product id and silently uninstalls an installed tsv first (its files, PATH entry and menu entries; not its data, which Janus takes over).
Internal names: JANUS_RENDERER, JANUS_VERSION, JANUS_ZEIT_PYTHON/BRIDGE, janus_zeit_bridge.py, resources/janus.*, installer/janus.iss.
CI runs the jn link of the Linux package and jn.com --version on Windows.

blocks.p: map panels side by side

ul: View > New map view: more map panels next to the main one, each with a layer and, if wanted, its own date and display mode; all on the same area (pan/zoom in any moves all), cursor mirrored, pins and ROI in all.
Several panels asking for tiles of the same layer no longer drop each other's requests (TileManager::tick once per frame).

blocks.p: mouse wheel zoom on macOS

ul: A mouse wheel zooms even with smooth scrolling (e.g. Logitech MX): only scrolls with gesture phases (trackpad, Magic Mouse) pan the map.
Wheel zoom is animated toward a target scale around the cursor, so a wheel that sends few, large steps zooms smoothly.
package_macos retries hdiutil create ("Resource busy" on CI runners).

blocks.p: relative paths in the macOS app; pins and fit shortcut on the Mac

ul: Inside an .app, glfwInit made Contents/Resources the current folder, so relative inputs (tsv folder/ from a terminal) failed to open (GLFW_COCOA_CHDIR_RESOURCES off). CI now runs the packaged programs from another folder with a relative input.
macOS: Control + click on a pin removes it (the Mac's right click; it no longer adds a pin). A two-finger click still works as the right click.
H fits the map to the window (was Home, which Mac keyboards lack).

blocks.p: macOS app, installers for every platform built by CI

ul: package_macos: tsv.app in a .dmg (drag to Applications). GDAL's library chain in Contents/Frameworks, PROJ/GDAL data and the Zeit runtime in Contents/Resources (platform::resourceDir), ad hoc signature, document types: folders and rasters open from the Finder (application:openURLs:, added to GLFW's delegate), at launch or while running.
macOS deployment target 15.0 (the Zeit runtime's wheels need it).

GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/build.yml): Windows, Linux and macOS builds; Zeit self-test everywhere, UI self-test on Linux (Xvfb + Mesa); the Windows installer is installed silently and tested, the Linux package and the app in the .dmg are run. A v* tag publishes the three installers as a GitHub Release.
tools/make_selftest_data.py (the self-test inputs); tools/make_icon.py also writes tsv.icns.
Chart: every Zeit tool result (fits, segments, breaks) is drawn in one colour no series uses, magenta with a dark outline.

blocks.p: categorical series; Mann-Kendall out of the statistics table

ul: Categorical detection: a colour table, category names or an attribute table on the band, or only a few whole values on the first date read; the Display panel can switch it off or force it.

Class colours from the file or a qualitative palette (no repeated colour when a class only appears later), drawn through a value -> colour lookup texture; editable legend (colour, name, visibility, share).
Chart as steps with class names on the Y axis; class statistics (class at the date, majority class, changes, last change); class name in the status bar.
The statistics table no longer computes Mann-Kendall (Z, p, trend): the full test is the Zeit tool. Sen's slope stays.
--selftest-ui takes categorical series with and without a colour table.

blocks.p: Linux build, POSIX Zeit processes and a portable Linux package

ul: Builds on Linux from a conda-forge environment (compiler, GDAL, X11/OpenGL headers); GDAL 3.13 metadata type fix.
ZeitProcess on POSIX: posix_spawn, close-on-exec pipes, the same filtered environment as on Windows, stderr to the log, SIGKILL to cancel.
platform on Linux/macOS: zenity/kdialog (AppleScript on macOS) dialogs, xdg-open/open, HDD detection via /sys/dev/block, XDG data folder.
Zeit runtime for Linux and macOS from python-build-standalone (stripped, pinned checksums) with manylinux/macOS wheels; debug information stripped from native libraries.

package_linux target: portable tsv-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.xz with the GDAL library chain, PROJ/GDAL data, the runtime and a .desktop file; RPATH $ORIGIN/lib. Tested in a clean environment: UI and Zeit self-tests pass.

blocks.p: TWDTW classification from pins and smoothing

ul: TWDTW (Zeit): classes are reference series taken from pins or the ROI mean and named in the tool window (new "patterns" parameter type). Outputs a class map, the best distance and the margin to the second class.
Class maps: outputs with "classes_param" carry the class names; each class gets a colour of a qualitative colormap, with a legend in the Layers panel and the class name in the status bar.
Smoothing (Zeit's Whittaker and Savitzky-Golay) on the chart.
--selftest-zeit fills "patterns" parameters from three pixels.
platform::localTime replaces localtime_s in shared code.

blocks.p: run-time estimates and Zeit fits on every layer

ul: Tool windows show the estimated computing time for the chosen scope. The bridge's new "estimate" method times the tool on growing samples of the series (after a warm-up call) and fits a fixed cost per block plus a cost per pixel, which matters for tools such as LandTrendr (~1 s per call).
With "All visible layers" on the chart, single-band tools are also fitted to the other layers' cursor and pin series, with their own dates.
Bridge input reading shared by jobs and estimates (Inputs class); --selftest-zeit compares each estimate with the real run.

blocks.p: several bands per date, phenology and CCDC

ul: One file per date with several bands: show a band or the normalized difference of two, and mask unusable observations with a quality band (Fmask codes, Landsat C2 QA_PIXEL bits or a 0/1 mask; detected by name). Display panel > Bands; applying reopens the layer in place, keeping its position, name, pins, view and results.
Bridge protocol for multiband tools: band roles, Fmask codes, real dates and what the layer shows; tsv reads the pixel's bands in the background and writes one VRT per band for raster jobs.
Phenology (season start, peak, end, length, amplitude) and CCDC (break dates, magnitude, NDVI change, segment models drawn in the shown units).
Performance panel hidden by default (View > Performance); Layers/Files above Display in the default layout.
Self-tests: --selftest-ui takes an optional multiband folder (automatic QA, NDVI reopen in place); --selftest-zeit covers the multiband tools.

blocks.p: Mann-Kendall and the BFAST family from Zeit

ul: Bridge split into a core (protocol, registry, chunked raster runner) and one module per tool family (zeit_bridge/tool_*.py); a broken module is reported in the manifest without hiding the others.
Mann-Kendall (original, Hamed-Rao, Yue-Wang, seasonal) with Sen's slope: Sen's line on the chart; significant slope, slope, p, Z, tau, trend class and intercept maps.
BFAST, BFAST Lite and BFAST Monitor: break dates drawn as vertical lines on the chart (new "vlines" overlay); break count, date and magnitude maps.
Manifest requirements "regular" (evenly spaced dates) and min_per_year, checked by tsv with the reason shown.
--selftest-zeit runs every tool that applies to the series (pixel run and a 256x256 raster job) and checks every output.
Bridge scripts are copied by their own CMake target, so editing a tool no longer needs the executable to relink.

blocks.p: feat: workspace with layers, files panel and detachable panels (0.5.0)

ul: Several series open at once as layers (File > Add layer, Ctrl+L, Files panel). Map space is the active layer's grid; the other layers are placed through their geotransforms (same CRS, no rotation) and are shown only when active otherwise, with the reason in the Layers panel. Each layer keeps its own mode, colormap, range and date; the others follow the active layer's date (nearest). Switching the active layer keeps the geographic view and remaps the pins.
Layers panel, always visible: show/hide (including the first series), order, opacity, close; Zeit results listed under their series
Chart and statistics for the active layer or every visible layer (cursor and pins of each layer, one marker shape per layer, each with its dates)
Files panel: folder tree listed in the background, rasters only by default, recent folders, open or add as a layer, multiple selection
Detachable panels (Dear ImGui multi-viewports), e.g. the map on a second monitor
"Layer" panel renamed to Display; new default layout (layout-0.5.ini)
--selftest-ui drives the layers workflow in a hidden window and checks the alignment, both layers' series and map pixels, without mouse or keyboard
build_zeit_runtime.py assembles into a staging folder and swaps it in at the end, so a failed build or a runtime in use is never left half-deleted
macOS core-profile hint; portability notes in IDEIAS.md

blocks.p: feat: Zeit tools in tsv, starting with LandTrendr (0.4.0)
Zeit (sacridini/zeit-cdts) runs in a separate Python process from a private runtime bundled with the installer, so end users need no Python or conda.

ul: tools/build_zeit_runtime.py assembles the runtime: embeddable Python 3.12, Zeit 0.25.0 from PyPI (--no-deps) and pinned dependencies without PyTorch; test suites are pruned and site-packages is kept short for the Windows path limit

zeit_bridge/tsv_zeit_bridge.py (Zeit itself is untouched): "serve" answers the tool manifest and per-pixel calls (JSON lines); "job" runs a tool on a raster window in its own process with progress (cancel = terminate)
Zeit client: windowless child processes inheriting only their own handles, clean environment for the bundled runtime, started in the background once a series is open (never on the startup path)

Tools menu built from the manifest; tool window with generated parameter form, applicability check, live fit on the chart and raster runs (whole image, visible area or ROI); Tasks panel with progress and cancel

LandTrendr: fitted segments drawn over the cursor, pin and ROI series, with the model's rows in the statistics table; raster outputs (year, magnitude, duration, pre/post value, rate, DSNR) loaded as map layers with their own colormap, range and opacity
tsv writes the cube as a VRT for Zeit (date order, nodata and scale applied)
Zooming out stops at the image extent
--selftest-zeit runs the whole path without a window; --zeit-python and --zeit-bridge point tsv at a developer environment
Installer bundles the runtime, warms it up after installing and refuses installation folders that are too long

blocks.p: feat: tsv 0.3.0 - raster time series viewer
Initial import of the viewer previously developed as rs_gui, renamed to tsv and translated to English.

ul: GPU cube overview (texture array) with on-disk cache; per-pixel temporal statistics in a shader; 10 map modes, colormaps, histogram
Full-resolution detail tiles with a GPU LRU cache
Exact pixel series under the cursor, pins, rectangular ROI with p10-p90
Series statistics: OLS, Sen's slope, Mann-Kendall; CSV export
Chart styles, anomaly/z-score views, per-series OLS/Sen trend lines
HDD detection with a single sequential reader; random reads deferred while the overview builds
Metadata of the inputs is read in the background: first frame in ~150 ms even when opening a cube; --measure-startup prints startup timings
Windows installer (Inno Setup), icon, console launcher (tsv.com), bundled GDAL runtime
README and IDEIAS.md (ideas, decisions and roadmap)
